weakest_inference: The single weakest link is the Case-B (n>=3) existence step in sufficiency: 'the open interval (a, a+c) has length c > theta, hence contains a theta-multiple m*theta, and this m lies in {1,...,n-1} so that the complementary angle 180 - m*theta = (n-m)*theta is also a valid (<=n-1)-fold multiple.' I attacked it directly with the construction m = floor(a/theta)+1 (which gives m*theta > a and m*theta <= a+theta < a+c, strictly interior) over an exhaustive rational grid (step 1/50 deg) and 362,999 random samples for many theta including 180/7: ZERO failures, and m always landed in {1,...,n-1} when (a,a+c) subset (0,180). The claim is equivalent to 'an open interval avoiding every multiple of theta must fit inside a single gap [j*theta,(j+1)*theta], hence has length <= theta' (contrapositive), which is rigorous. It holds; this is not a gap, just the most analysis-flavored step and stated most briefly in the candidate text.

summary: Second-order audit CONFIRMS the candidate's answer: Mulan guarantees victory iff theta divides 180 degrees, i.e. theta = 180/n for an integer n >= 2. I independently re-derived and attacked every link. NECESSITY (theta does not divide 180 => Mulan loses): the trap S = {triangles with no theta-multiple angle} is non-empty (equilateral, since theta|60 would force theta|180) and closed under Shan-Yu's reply via a complete, arithmetically sound four-case analysis (each case derives a contradiction from theta-multiples being closed under integer sum/difference); the equilateral-seeded defending strategy keeps the state theta-multiple-free forever, so no angle is ever theta. SUFFICIENCY (theta=180/n => Mulan wins): the Lemma that any triangle with a k*theta angle (1<=k<=n-1) is winning is proven by a well-founded strong induction (split the k*theta angle into theta+(k-1)theta; one piece is terminal, the kept piece carries a (k-1)*theta angle, strictly lower index); Case A applies it directly, Case B (no multiple angle) splits the largest angle c with c1 = m*theta - a (m = smallest multiple index exceeding a), placing m*theta in one piece and the complementary (n-m)*theta in the other, both winning -- the only non-trivial existence fact (interval of length > theta contains a multiple) is rigorously verified by construction and exhaustive/random testing with zero failures; the n=2 (theta=90) edge is handled separately and correctly. A uniform finite bound of <= n-1 cuts is established and confirmed tight in simulation (0 violations over 54,000 trials). No circular dependencies (Lemma is self-contained; Cases A/B depend only on it; necessity and sufficiency are independent). I specifically tried to overturn via the discriminator theta=72 (divides 360 not 180 -> NOT all-winning, confirming 'divides 180'), via equilateral-as-trap for 15 distinct non-divisors (no escape cut exists), and via the interval-contains-multiple inference (no counterexample in 362,999+ samples). No fatal gap, no hidden quantifier shift, no degenerate-case hole, no circularity found. The numerical section is supplementary and the proof stands without it. Agreement with the first reviewer is noted but not used as evidence; all conclusions rest on my own re-derivation and computation.
